correctness.rationale: For the intrinsic metric on {r<=|x|<=R}, shortest paths are chords when unobstructed and two tangents plus a shorter inner-circle arc when obstructed. With K=R^2-r^2 and g(s)=sqrt(s^2-r^2)-r arccos(r/s), monotonicity in radius and minor angle gives exact diameter 2sqrt(K)+2r atan(r/sqrt(K)). The small-distance area coefficient equals 1/K, and the diameter strictly increases in r at fixed K, proving inverse radii uniqueness. For r>0 the near-diameter loss is c(R-rho)+c(R-sigma)+r(pi-theta)+quadratic remainder, c=sqrt(K)/R. Three independent scaled defects have limiting constant density 4R^4/(pi rK^3), and simplex volume 1/6 gives the precise cubic upper-tail coefficient 2R^4/(3pi rK^3) and a uniform-simplex mark law. When r=a sqrt(R epsilon), the chord/tangent boundary occurs at z=2a; the limiting loss is x+y+F_a(z), F_a(z)=az below 2a and a^2+z^2/4 above. Integrating its x,y sections produces J(a), piecewise with threshold a=1/sqrt(2), including disk a=0 and conditional density 2/J(a). Analytic localization/tightness supplies dominated convergence only for fixed a. Independent symbolic integration of J verified the exact two branches and their joining; finite quadrature was not mistaken for the proof.
residual_risks: A finite verifier is supporting evidence rather than proof of the complete infinite statement.
